title: Give your coding agent a short map instead of a long manual
summary: A team cut each service's main Claude Code instruction file from 238 to about 80 lines and let the agent pick which detail files to read; they noticed fewer tokens used.
agent_role: The agent decides how complex each task is and reads only the matching detail files. Humans wrote the short map, the level rule and the detail docs.
outcome: Authors report the agent started using fewer tokens, especially on work spanning several services.
what_they_did: A team with dozens of services had a long instruction file in each one, loaded on every request. They cut it to a short map with a four-level rule: a typo needs only the map, while cross-service work also needs integration and architecture notes. The agent picks the level itself.
how_it_went: They say each root file shrank from about 238 lines to about 80, roughly 900 fewer tokens per request. They noticed lower token use, especially in cross-service development.
worth_knowing: The map only works if the detail files stay current; a stale integrations file will mislead the agent. The agent can also choose the wrong level.
prompt: Read the main instruction file in [project folder] and the docs it covers. Propose a short version, under 80 lines, that works as a map: what lives where, plus a simple rule for which extra files to read by task size (small fix, one module, several modules, cross-service). Move the detail into separate files in [docs folder]. Show me the new map and file layout before changing anything.

curation.rationale: A concrete setup for steering a coding agent across many services with a short index file and four task levels, but results are only loosely described.
